messages.subject: inla.spde2.result
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to understand the output of inla.spde2.result. Following the example in the manual:

loc = matrix(runif(100*2),100,2)
mesh = inla.mesh.create.helper(points.domain=loc, max.edge=c(0.1,0.5))
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh)
index = inla.spde.make.index("spatial", mesh$n, n.repl=2)
spatial.A = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc,
                             index=rep(1:nrow(loc), 2),
                             repl=rep(1:2, each=nrow(loc)))
## Toy example with no spatial correlation (range=zero)
y = 10+rnorm(100*2)
stack = inla.stack(data=list(y=y),
                   A=list(spatial.A),
                   effects=list(c(index, list(intercept=1))),
                   tag="tag")
data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde)
formula = y ~ -1 + intercept + f(spatial, model=spde,
                                 replicate=spatial.repl)
result = inla(formula, family="gaussian", data=data, 
              control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack)))
spde.result = inla.spde2.result(result, "spatial", spde)


I found that the "user friendly" results and expected values calculated from the marginals do not match, for example:

c(exp(spde.result$summary.log.kappa$mean), inla.emarginal(identity, spde.result$marginals.kappa[[1]])) # Not the same
tau <- exp(spde.result$summary.log.tau$mean)
kappa <- exp(spde.result$summary.log.kappa$mean)
c(sqrt(8)/kappa, exp(spde.result$summary.log.range.nominal$mean)) # The same
c(1/(4*pi*tau^2*kappa^2), exp(spde.result$summary.log.variance.nominal$mean)) # Not the same

What am I missing?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.spde2.result
parts:
On 05/02/14 07:58, Jussi wrote:
> I found that the "user friendly" results and expected values calculated
> from the marginals do not match, for example:
>
> c(exp(spde.result$summary.log.kappa$mean), inla.emarginal(identity,
> spde.result$marginals.kappa[[1]])) # Not the same

Let g(theta) be a linear functional of a vector-valued theta.
Then
exp(E(g(theta)|Y)) is _not_ the same thing as E(exp(g(theta))|Y)
so they _should_ not match. (And Jensen's inequality says that
the first is smaller than the second, which is precisely what we get.)

> tau <- exp(spde.result$summary.log.tau$mean)
> kappa <- exp(spde.result$summary.log.kappa$mean)
> c(sqrt(8)/kappa, exp(spde.result$summary.log.range.nominal$mean)) # The same

Yes, and here they should match, since both are exp(E(g(theta)|Y)), and
computed in the same way.

Here, you _are_ right that the results should be the same, in theory.

The difference likely occurs due to the skewness of the
distributions; The error can be expected to be smaller when directly
approximating the distribution for log(variance) than approximating
log(tau) and log(kappa) separately and then summing their respective
expectations, but I'm surprised that the difference seems to be so
noticeable.

Finn L

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.spde2.result
parts:
we have prior effect here.
Wen we believe on no spatial effect,
we can include it.

##For example, using:
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh,
prior.variance.nominal=0.1,
prior.range.nominal=0.1)
##we have very different results.
## or just it:
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh, prior.range.nominal=0.05)

##As we have very skew posterior distributions,
##instead to look at posterior mean,
##we have better understanding on figures

par(mfrow=c(2,2), mar=c(3,3,1,0.5))
plot(spde.result$marginals.variance.nominal[[1]], type='l')
plot(spde.result$marginals.kappa[[1]], type='l')
plot(spde.result$marginals.range.nominal[[1]], type='l')

best,
Elias.
